simple.meaning: טְלָאִים (Ṭᵉlâʼîym) is a Hebrew word meaning “Telaim , a place in Palestine.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: This word has limited occurrence data, so BibleIQ begins with the Hebrew word, its basic meaning, and the verse where it appears.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to טְלָאִים (H2923) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in טְלָאִים (H2923) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: טְלָאִים (Ṭᵉlâʼîym) / H2923 is traced through 1 Samuel 15:4 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H2923. Telaim I. טְלָאִים proper name, of a location with article ׳הַטְּל , place where Saul mustered his forces 1Sam 15:4 , probably = טֶלֶם q. v. II. טְלָאִים see following. טלה (√ of following; meaning dubious; Arabic , is tie a lamb to a stake, confine ; Syriac is make young , both apparently denominative; Lag Armen. Stud. § 2229 finds earlier form of טָלֶה in Armenian).

occurrences.englishText: Saul summoned the people, and counted them in Telaim, two hundred thousand footmen, and ten thousand men of Judah.
